c3e29c11fce5.text: Hi! Let's explore how a camera's position changes a picture. We'll start at eye level, then look from below and above. Grab something to draw with, and let's have fun.

20ab025a480e.text: Let's start with a normal shot. The camera is at the same height as our friend's eyes. Look at the camera on the left, then see its picture on the right.

0cb3488297b5.text: Start with a simple face and two eyes. See how the horizon line passes right through the eyes? In this scene, our camera and our friend's eyes are at the same height.

2d819ca322b5.text: This purple dot is the vanishing point. Drag it gently left and right along the horizon. Watch how the lines guide us into the space.

d34f09fd273c.text: Now follow the lines away from the vanishing point. They help us place the road and pavement. Keep your pencil lines light.

bc806775ef20.text: Let's add our characters. Start with their feet on the ground, then add a head, body and a few simple lines. The friend farther away looks smaller.

6112e808307d.text: Add a little background: a couple of buildings and a tree. Keep it simple, so we can still see what our character is doing.

017297428eea.text: This is our teacher's quick-sketch reference step. Watch the sketch when it's available, then give it a try yourself. Have fun, and make it your own.

4a171809c6b3.text: Now it's your turn! A friend faces you on the right-hand pavement. Small houses, a tree and an alley frame the street. Use a simple stick figure, or invent your own character. Take your time, and have fun!

cdd7db6e635e.text: This building faces two directions, so we use two vanishing points on the same horizon. One may be outside the picture. Drag the purple point and watch the lines change.

341b834b4fa2.text: Follow the two directions around the building's corner. Each set of parallel edges leads toward its own vanishing point.

c8fe38090a9b.text: Now it's your turn! A student turns sideways to say hi. Another classmate approaches, with distant hills behind the street corner. Use a simple stick figure, or invent your own character. Take your time, and have fun!

c2bbe4b773a7.text: Let's open up the room. Follow the floor and wall edges toward the vanishing point. Try a few light lines on your paper.

9f2956eb573c.text: Place a simple person inside the room, with their feet on the floor. A circle and a few lines are enough. You can use your own character style.

ec1e9d683320.text: Add a desk and a shelf. Follow the room's perspective lines. Just a few simple shapes will tell us where we are.

a697277779f9.text: Now it's your turn! A friend stands beside a desk. The floor and walls lead toward one vanishing point. Use a simple stick figure, or invent your own character. Take your time, and have fun!

40536d6958ae.text: Now let's try a low angle. The camera moves down and looks gently upward. Compare the camera's position with the picture beside it.

59f659c33bcb.text: Begin with a simple head. Our camera is lower than the person's eyes, so the camera's horizon does not pass through their eyes this time.

aedad0e00a88.text: Now it's your turn! From a low camera, a friend raises a hand. The houses rise behind them. Use a simple stick figure, or invent your own character. Take your time, and have fun!

2bfd255bb3c7.text: Now it's your turn! Look up at a classmate greeting a friend at the corner of the school building. Use a simple stick figure, or invent your own character. Take your time, and have fun!

ab7628f2aec3.text: Now it's your turn! From near the floor, watch a student reach toward a high shelf. Use a simple stick figure, or invent your own character. Take your time, and have fun!

d28bedff796b.text: Let's look from a high angle. The camera is above our friend, looking gently down. Notice the head and the ground around the figure.

4097cae05196.text: Begin with a simple head. The camera is higher than our friend's eyes. Notice how the horizon and the person's eyes are at different heights.

6985ad478e75.text: Now it's your turn! Look down at a friend waving from the pavement. Follow the road into the distance. Use a simple stick figure, or invent your own character. Take your time, and have fun!

29693a3d0c75.text: Now it's your turn! From a higher landing, see two friends meeting near a building corner. Use a simple stick figure, or invent your own character. Take your time, and have fun!

375caf8beaf3.text: Now it's your turn! Look down at a student beside a desk, searching the classroom floor. Use a simple stick figure, or invent your own character. Take your time, and have fun!

326b829a9afb.text: Let's bring it all together. A friend stops to say hello. Draw a small sketch at eye level. Keep the person and the setting simple.

ad8f22d0d6ad.text: Keep the same greeting, but move the camera lower. Draw a second little sketch looking up. Notice what feels different.

840a1f5d3a64.text: Now move the camera higher and look down. Draw your third sketch. Notice how much ground you can see around your friend.

a5d82f347636.text: Nice work! Put your three sketches side by side. Look at the ground and the character. What changed? Each viewpoint tells the story a little differently. Keep exploring, and have fun drawing!
